clue.text: Women's keenness for making approaches

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
a blade's keenness is its edge, as in 'take the edge off'

explanation.surface: A remark that women's eagerness is what drives them to make advances.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is golfing: a wedge is the lofted club a golfer uses for approach shots to the green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the lofted iron called by this name is the club chosen for short approach shots.

clue.text: Place known for tennis elbow — mind out!

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A warning about tennis elbow at the famous venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tennis elbow' looks like one injury; 'Place known for tennis' is the definition, and ELBOW MIND rearranged ('out') gives the London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-west London suburb hosts the most famous grass-court championship.

clue.text: Strong material dug up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dug as in dug for ore means mined

explanation.surface: Tough fabric found by digging.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, used for jeans, is a strong material.

clue.text: Making Bill work in the House …

explanation.surface: Getting a man named Bill a job in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a parliamentary bill being made law. The House is a theatre, where performing a role is acting it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a bill into law, and performing a part on stage before a theatre audience.

clue.text: Rubs clean in sink in this address

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to sink or fade away is to die, as a sound dies
to scour is to rub something clean

explanation.surface: Someone scrubbing in a kitchen sink at this house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sink' paints scrubbing at the kitchen sink, but 'sink' gives a word for fading away and 'in' is the container signal; 'this' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An address in the sense of a formal speech or talk is a synonym for a lecture of that kind.

clue.text: … charwoman having failed to finish lower chamber

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter of the word for a cleaner is dropped

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning lady who comes in each day

explanation.surface: A cleaner who never finished the downstairs room.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament; 'chamber' looks domestic but is legislative, following the House of 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish parliament's lower house, Dáil Éireann, is its elected assembly.

clue.text: Miss once?

parts.note: Miss is how pupils addressed a female teacher, and once points to an old-fashioned kind of village teacher

explanation.walkthrough: A dame school was a small private school run by an elderly woman in her home, common before state education in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman who ran a small old village school was addressed by pupils as their teacher.

clue.text: Capital ring taking a power unit over

parts.note: a ring is O, from its shape

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, read upwards

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

explanation.surface: A capital city's ring road taking over a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns A WATT into TTAWA, which follows O; 'taking' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ontario city is the seat of Canada's government, its capital.

clue.text: Carpet of corded material on edge and end

indicators.note: end tells us the word and goes at the end of the build

parts.note: rep is a ribbed or corded fabric
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A rug of ribbed fabric, bound along its edge and end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, to haul someone over the coals; 'on' is a link and 'end' puts AND last.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone, in British slang, is to rebuke them formally.

clue.text: Strange how huge lake engulfs head of Ennerdale

indicators.note: the lake engulfs, swallowing up, the letter taken from the Lake District name

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: How odd that a vast lake swallows the top of a small English lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Ennerdale Water is a small lake in the Lake District of north-west England; its first letter goes inside ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange and unsettling is weird or uncanny.

clue.text: Rev up like this after service, his dynamo needing repair?

definitions.text: Rev up like this after service

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters must be rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A man revs a car engine after a garage service, though his dynamo is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' is not engine talk but a clergyman: after Sunday services a vicar feels jaded, as people do on a Monday. The anagram of HIS DYNAMO, signalled by 'needing repair', gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman worn out by Sunday duties feels the weary, start-of-week mood named by this word.

clue.text: One who drinks like a fish, right?

parts.note: the tope is a small shark, a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone who drinks heavily is fairly described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks like a fish' reads as one idiom, but 'One who drinks' is the definition and 'a fish' is the tope; 'like' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy, habitual drinker is called by this old-fashioned word.

clue.text: Edges of motorway, illuminated on both sides, going to the south

indicators.note: the illuminated word stands on both sides of the motorway, wrapping round it

parts.note: illuminated means lit
MI stands for the M1, Britain's first motorway

explanation.surface: Describing a motorway lit along both sides as it heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges of motorway' looks like hard shoulders; 'Edges' alone is the definition. The motorway is the M1, London to Leeds, written MI; 'on both sides' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries or outer bounds of an area are its edges, as in the bounds of a city.

clue.text: Short hair-style, without colour, makes an American quail

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
white can be taken as the absence of colour

explanation.surface: A short, bleached haircut somehow produces a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American game bird, named for its call, is a kind of quail.

clue.text: Get relief from cardialgia in bed

definitions.text: Get relief from cardialgia in bed

parts.words: Get relief from cardialgia in bed
parts.note: cardialgia is heart pain, so its easing, and the bed is a flower bed where a wild pansy grows

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a patient resting in bed; the bed is a garden bed and the relief is a flower whose name means comfort for the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy carries this old name, meaning comfort for the heart, and grows in garden beds.

clue.text: Vague suggestion, we hear, of making less noise in bars

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: a vague suggestion is a dim innuendo

explanation.surface: A faint hint that a pub should quieten down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs, but these are bars of music, where a passage grows gradually quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this term marks a gradual decrease in loudness across a passage.

clue.text: Promises of a party in show-ring

parts.note: to manifest is to show
O is a ring, from its shape

explanation.surface: A party's pledges displayed in a show-ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show-ring' looks like one arena; split it as show plus ring, with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its pledges in a programme document before an election.

clue.text: Deposit from ground-rent

parts.note: reads like money paid on leased land, but a rent is a split, so this is what is left by matter erupting from a split in the earth

explanation.walkthrough: Ground-rent is a lease payment in Britain; here 'rent' means a tear or fissure, and the 'deposit' is molten rock that solidifies after flowing from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock flowing from a volcanic fissure cools into a deposit of this name.

clue.text: Having excellence in lofty environment?

indicators.note: lofty environment means the word for lofty surrounds, forming the environment of, the excellence

parts.note: airy can mean high and lofty
worth is merit or excellence

explanation.surface: Asking whether something has merit high up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: 'lofty environment' surrounds the excellence, and something fit to fly has excellence up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft certified as fit to fly is sound enough for the skies.

clue.text: Fresh, like bather off Cowes

explanation.surface: A cheeky swimmer off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a town on the Isle of Wight, beside the Solent strait; someone swimming there is in the Solent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky or impudent, as in being fresh with someone; and someone swimming in the strait off Cowes is in it.

clue.text: Some' — often unseen dedicated women

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some dedicated women are seldom seen by outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who have dedicated their lives to a religious order are sisters in convents.

clue.text: Concert-goer at the front

explanation.surface: A music lover standing right at the front of the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Promenade concerts (the Proms) are London's summer concert series; 'the front' is the seaside esplanade, where people stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attends the Proms, the London summer concert season, or one who strolls along a seafront esplanade.

clue.text: Boxes or spars after assembly

explanation.surface: A boxer who spars after a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' and 'spars' look like boxing; they are packing cases and wooden poles that, nailed together, make them.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing cases are boxes, and slatted wooden cases are what lengths of timber become once put together.

clue.text: Remove Dean, being improperly fostered?

indicators.note: improperly means the letters are arranged wrongly and must be put right

explanation.surface: A clergyman removed from office after being wrongly placed in foster care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' is not a cleric but the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire; to remove that forest is to strip land of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing away the Forest of Dean would mean cutting down its trees, stripping the land of woodland.

clue.text: Sort of language typical of some columnists

explanation.surface: A writing style typical of certain newspaper columnists.
explanation.walkthrough: Doric is the broad Scots dialect of north-east Scotland; it is also the plainest of the classical orders of columns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic Scots dialect, and the simplest classical order of architecture used for columns.

clue.text: Cloak and mask, usually with spots

explanation.surface: A masked figure in a cloak, a dotted costume perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded masquerade cloak worn with a half-mask, and a game tile normally marked with pips.

clue.text: Man embracing young Diana has peculiar expression

indicators.note: embracing means the island holds the short name inside it

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man
Di is a short, familiar form of Diana

explanation.surface: A man hugging a girl called Diana pulls an odd face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase peculiar to a language, whose sense cannot be read from its words, is a turn of speech.

clue.text: Racecourse without a tax

indicators.note: without means the letter is taken away

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A racecourse that charges no tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot hosts Royal Ascot, Britain's grand summer race meeting; scot is an old word for a levy, as in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: An old levy or payment, surviving in the phrase scot-free, was a local tax.

clue.text: Military band to arrange pieces afresh

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British military corps
a band or group of people is a set

explanation.surface: A military band arranging pieces of music anew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military band' looks like one musical unit, and 'pieces' like music; the pieces are those on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: To put chess pieces back in position, or any items into place again, is to set them up once more.

clue.text: The claims he made for his elixirs!

definitions.text: The claims he made for his elixirs!

indicators.note: made here means the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Scepticism about the boasts of a quack selling potions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: the letters of THE CLAIMS rearranged give the man who made such claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval practitioner who sought the philosopher's stone made extravagant boasts for his potions of life.

clue.text: Look out here, they say, for high tars

definitions.text: Look out here, they say, for high tars

parts.words: Look out here, they say, for high tars
parts.note: a warning to keep watch reads also as the place on a ship where sailors keep watch, perched high on the mast

explanation.walkthrough: Tars are sailors; the lookout post at the top of a ship's mast is where a lookout sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at the masthead of a sailing ship is named after a bird's high perch.

clue.text: Medal clasped by model soldier

indicators.note: clasped by means the medal is held inside the model

parts.note: a toy is a model, as in a toy soldier
MM is the Military Medal, a British award

explanation.surface: A model soldier holding a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model soldier' reads as one toy; 'soldier' is the definition, a Tommy being the nickname of a British private.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy is the traditional nickname for an ordinary British private soldier.
